candidate.title: Contextual suitability of digital interventions
candidate.summary: Parked historical direction: an AI-assisted assessment of whether digital interventions are suitable for the Ghanaian public/population context. It was deprioritised because the proposed work risked becoming social-science-heavy and did not yet demonstrate a distinct IT contribution.
candidate.shortDescription: A record of the earlier Policy Friction Score / digital-policy suitability concept and why it is not currently a preferred MPhil topic.
candidate.ghanaianRelevance: The earlier setting was institutional and Ghanaian. That does not repair the unit-of-analysis problem.
candidate.technicalContribution: The earlier concept proposed a Design Science Research artefact: a computational decision-support approach to assess population-level friction or readiness for digital policies. It is not an active contribution claim; the supervisor’s concern about a social-science-heavy framing remains unresolved.

feasibility.rationale: This is a planning assessment. The direction should not proceed on the current framing.

candidate.dataRequirements: Earlier discussions considered individual-level Afrobarometer data and Ghana Statistical Service data, with institutional context as supplementary evidence. The unit of analysis was intended to be the public/population rather than organisations. Data availability, construct compatibility, sample size, and the mapping from survey measures to computational inputs were not resolved.
candidate.evaluationDesign: The earlier design considered AHP, CRITIC, and TOPSIS for weighting/ranking, with computational checks for numerical precision to 1×10^-6, zero variance, identical districts, missing data, all-deficiency-flag cases, and clean-environment reproducibility with fixed seeds. These are retained as historical design notes, not a recommendation to resume the topic.
majorRisks: Supervisor feedback was that the earlier topic looked too much like a software-development project and risked becoming social-science-heavy rather than a rigorous MPhil IT thesis.
Existing readiness frameworks may already cover the proposed dimensions.
The relationship between population-level survey data and policy-level suitability scores needs a defensible unit of analysis.
A weighted score could create an artefact without a sufficiently original computing contribution.
openDecisions: Keep parked unless a distinct computational research contribution, defensible unit of analysis, and evaluation baseline are established.
If reconsidered, demonstrate what the computational method adds beyond existing readiness frameworks and standard multi-criteria decision analysis.

nodes.title: Suitability of a digital intervention is easy to overclaim
nodes.summary: Asking whether a digital intervention fits its context can collapse into a social survey unless the computational contribution is explicit.
nodes.detail: The earlier idea was an AI-assisted decision-support system or Policy Friction Score for assessing whether digital policies/interventions are suitable for the Ghanaian public/population. The unit of analysis was intended to be individuals/population rather than organisations. The idea considered adoption-related constructs such as trust, self-efficacy, anxiety, and perceived usefulness, alongside infrastructure and institutional context. It is retained for traceability but parked after supervisor feedback that the proposal risked being a software-development project and becoming social-science-heavy rather than a strong IT thesis.

nodes.title: Can a computational policy-suitability assessment add defensible information beyond existing readiness frameworks?
nodes.summary: Which measurable factors predict suitability for one narrow class of digital intervention, beyond existing readiness frameworks?
nodes.detail: This was the historical question behind the Policy Friction Score. It is not an active thesis question. The original challenge is to show a technically meaningful computational contribution and a valid unit of analysis, rather than merely combining survey constructs into another score.

nodes.title: Kept as a warning, not a candidate to build
nodes.summary: The earlier concept had unresolved originality, data-unit, and method problems.
nodes.detail: The original motivation was Ghanaian digital-policy implementation and the risk that interventions become “white elephants” when they do not fit population context. The broader project preference remains that IT should be context-aware and useful. This motivation alone does not establish an MPhil IT contribution.

nodes.title: A Ghanaian institutional setting was the earlier context
nodes.summary: A Ghanaian institutional setting was the earlier context
nodes.detail: The earlier concept referred to Ghanaian institutions. Public country indicators still cannot be treated as observations of those institutions.

nodes.title: An IT contribution is not currently stated
nodes.summary: An IT contribution is not currently stated
nodes.detail: Trust, self-efficacy, and anxiety scales are not, by themselves, a computing method. A decision-support or measurement model would need a separate technical evaluation.

nodes.title: No contribution is claimed
nodes.detail: No differentiated measurement model is proposed. The entry records why the earlier concept should stay parked.

nodes.title: A unit of analysis
nodes.detail: Historical design requirement: define the unit of analysis as individuals/population, not organisations, and specify how individual-level observations map to the policy/intervention being assessed.

nodes.title: A comparison with an existing framework
nodes.summary: A comparison with an existing framework
nodes.detail: Historical comparison requirement: compare any proposed Policy Friction Score against existing readiness/adoption frameworks and demonstrate incremental information rather than assuming a new composite score is novel.

nodes.title: A technical evaluation
nodes.detail: Historical computational validation plan: test AHP, CRITIC, and TOPSIS calculations to 1×10^-6; test zero-variance inputs, identical districts/units, missing data, all-deficiency-flag cases, and reproducibility from a clean environment with fixed seeds.

nodes.title: Whether this is still an IT thesis
nodes.summary: Whether this is still an IT thesis
nodes.detail: Readiness frameworks already cover technical, human, organisational, and policy factors. A new questionnaire is not automatically a computing contribution.

nodes.title: Existing readiness frameworks use similar dimensions
nodes.summary: Existing readiness frameworks use similar dimensions
nodes.detail: Earlier versions combined technology-adoption constructs (including TAM/UTAUT-related measures, trust, self-efficacy, and anxiety) with infrastructure and institutional context. The project considered Afrobarometer individual-level data and Ghana Statistical Service data; institutional context was supplementary. The literature and construct compatibility were not fully reconciled.

nodes.title: A further readiness score may not add a computational result
nodes.summary: A further readiness score may not add a computational result
nodes.detail: The central unresolved question was whether a new Policy Friction Score would add a computational result beyond existing readiness/adoption frameworks. A further concern was whether available public survey data could validly represent population readiness for a particular digital intervention. The supervisor’s feedback was a framing warning, not evidence of a literature gap.
risks: Country-level indicators are not institution-level observations.
Sample size, data access, and framework novelty were unresolved in the earlier concept.
validationRequirements: Identify an existing baseline framework and compare incremental value.
Validate the unit of analysis and construct-to-data mapping.
Do not treat country-level or institutional indicators as individual-level observations.
Show technical novelty beyond implementing a weighted score.

nodes.title: Park this direction unless a computational method is specified
nodes.summary: Park this direction unless a computational method is specified
nodes.detail: Status: parked. Do not resume simply because public survey data or questionnaire collection appears accessible. Reconsider only if a distinct computational method, unit of analysis, baseline, and rigorous technical evaluation can be demonstrated.
